transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. Can you start by telling me what brings you in today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Well, the main reason I'm here is that I'm having a really hard time at work. I'm a nurse, and on the floor, I just lose my train of thought constantly. It's like... an IV pump will beep, or I'll overhear someone asking another nurse a question, or a call light goes off, and suddenly I've completely forgotten what patient flow issue I was just working on. It's happening so much, and I just really need to figure out what's going on.
Have you noticed this kind of difficulty staying focused going back to childhood or your school years, or is this something that started more recently in your adult life?

It's definitely not new. Even back in elementary school, my teachers would always write on my report cards that I was bright, but careless. I was just always losing my worksheets or... completely forgetting to turn in my homework. My mom actually had to sit with me every single night while I did my work just to keep me on track. So, yeah, it's been an issue for a long time.
Aside from the trouble staying focused, have you been feeling persistently anxious, worried, or down in your mood lately?

No, not really. I mean, I get stressed out when I fall behind at work because of the distraction stuff, but I wouldn't say I feel anxious or worried in general. And my mood is fine. I'm not feeling down or depressed or anything like that. It's really just the focus issues that are getting in the way.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble sitting still, or find yourself acting impulsively—like interrupting others or making quick decisions without thinking them through?

No, I don't think so. I don't really have trouble sitting still or feel restless. I'm actually pretty calm physically. And I wouldn't say I'm impulsive or that I interrupt people, either. It's really just the mental part for me—my mind just completely wanders off, but I don't have that physical restlessness or impulsivity you're talking about.
Does this difficulty with focus and forgetfulness also cause problems for you outside of work, like at home or in your personal relationships?

Yes, it definitely does. It affects a lot of things at home, too. I just... I forget things that should be completely routine. Like, I'll forget to call a family member back, or I won't follow up on a missing order. Paying a bill at home, or even just showing up for a personal appointment—it just slips my mind. 

And the frustrating part is that I fully mean to do these things. It's not that I don't care. Sometimes I even set a reminder on my phone to do it, but... I still just end up forgetting anyway.
Have you noticed any problems with your sleep, such as difficulty falling or staying asleep, or do you use alcohol, caffeine, or other substances that might be affecting your concentration?

No, my sleep is pretty normal. I don't have any trouble falling asleep or staying asleep. And I don't really drink much—maybe a glass of wine on the weekend, but nothing crazy. I do drink coffee, just a cup or two in the morning before my shift, but that's it. I don't use any other substances or anything like that.
